title: Integrated Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, Revenue Recognition & Billing
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's core finance and legal procedures for budgeting & forecasting, procurement, contracts review, and revenue recognition/billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and budget-owning engineering/product stakeholders. The playbook defines roles, thresholds, step-by-step procedures, SLAs, and templates to ensure consistent, auditable decisions and timely execution.

Scope

- Applies to all spend, contract, and revenue activities for Redwood Inference (hosted, dedicated, private product lines).
- Covers: annual/quarterly budgeting, rolling forecasts, procurement (POs and vendor onboarding), contract intake & review, and revenue recognition & billing for usage, committed capacity, and enterprise arrangements.

Ownership and Roles

- Finance (Budget Owner): maintains company-wide budget, consolidates forecasts, approves spend above delegated thresholds.
- Legal (Contract Owner): responsible for contract review, risk assessment, and signatory tracking.
- Procurement (Procurement Ops): issues POs, manages vendor onboarding and vendor master data.
- Budget Owner (Service/Team): owns line-item forecasts, variance explanations, and request for reallocations.
- Revenue Accounting: maintains revrec schedules and billing rules.

Key SLOs and SLAs

- Contract review turnaround: Standard NDA/MSA review within 5 business days; complex enterprise contracts within 10 business days.
- PO issuance SLA: 3 business days from approved requisition for purchases < $50k; 7 business days for larger requests pending approvals.
- Budget refresh cadence: Quarterly rolling forecast with monthly updates.
- RevRec schedule updates: Within 10 business days of any material contract change.

Part A: Budgeting & Forecasting

1) Annual Budget Calendar (high level):
   - Sep–Oct: Strategic planning and headcount/major project requests due.
   - Nov: Finance consolidates target budget and leadership reviews.
   - Dec: Executive review and final budget approval.
   - Jan: Operationalization and allocation to team owners.

2) Rolling Forecast Process:
   - Monthly inputs from team owners into the rolling forecast workbook (Cloud storage: /finance/rolling-forecast).
   - Finance validates assumptions: utilization, ARR movement, committed capacity revenue, cloud spend, and GPUs.
   - Discrepancies > 10% flagged and require a variance memo.

3) Budget Change Requests (BCR):
   - Use the BCR form (Finance template link) for any reallocation > $25k or material headcount changes.
   - Approval path: Team lead -> Finance business partner -> VP Finance (if > $250k) -> CFO (if > $1M).

4) Budget Controls and Gateways:
   - All capital purchases > $50k require capex approval and schedule with finance.
   - Hiring must be routed through People Ops with budget code attached.

Part B: Procurement Procedures

Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:

| Request Type | Amount (USD) | Required Approvals | Procurement SLA |
|--------------|--------------|--------------------|-----------------|
| Operational Purchase | < $5k | Team Lead | 3 business days |
| Standard PO | $5k - $50k | Team Lead, Finance BP | 3 business days |
| Large Purchase | $50k - $250k | Director, Finance BP, Procurement | 7 business days |
| Strategic / Capital | > $250k | VP, Procurement, Legal, Finance | 10+ business days |

Procurement steps (numbered):

1. Requisition: Submit requisition in procurement system with budget code, vendor, SOW/quote, and expected delivery.
2. Review & Budget Check: Finance verifies available budget and assigns accounting codes.
3. Vendor Due Diligence: Procurement confirms vendor onboarding documents (W-9/LEI, insurance cert, security questionnaire for cloud vendors).
4. PO Issuance: Procurement issues PO and tracks acceptance.
4a. For card purchases under $5k, retain receipt and submit to finance within 5 business days.
5. Receipt & Invoice Processing: Receiving team confirms goods/services, routes invoice to AP with PO reference.

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Completed vendor profile in VendorMaster
- Tax forms (W-9 or equivalent)
- Insurance certificate (where applicable)
- Information security questionnaire and security contact for cloud vendors
- Signed Master Service Agreement (MSA) or standard terms where required

Part C: Contracts & Legal Process

Contract intake and review workflow:

1. Intake: Contracts are submitted via the Contract Intake form (Link) with contract type, counterparty, commercial terms, and redlines required.
2. Triage (Legal): Legal assigns risk level (Low/Medium/High) using template risk rubric. Low risk: standard SaaS MSA, NDA. Medium/High: revenue > $250k, PII/regulated data, or unusual indemnities.
3. Redline & Negotiation: Legal collaborates with commercial owner and finance for pricing clauses, payment terms, and termination.
4. Final Approvals: Signature authority table:
   - Legal Counsel: up to $250k commercial exposure
   - Head of Legal: $250k - $1M
   - CFO & CEO: > $1M or strategic commitments
5. Execution & Storage: Executed contracts stored in Contract Repository with indexed metadata (counterparty, start/end date, renewal terms).

Contract review checklist (short):
- Verify counterparty identity and contract owner
- Confirm scope of work and acceptance criteria
- Payment terms (Net 30/Net 45) and invoicing instructions
- Termination & renewal language and notice periods
- Liability and indemnity caps aligned to company policy
- Data protection & security addenda applied for vendor handling customer data

Expedited review exceptions:
- NDAs and low-risk renewals may use the self-service template; legal must be notified but formal review can be waived for time-sensitive deals (<48 hours) per documented rationale.

Part D: Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

General principles:
- Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, recognize when performance obligations satisfied.
- For Redwood products we commonly see: recurring hosted usage (metered), committed capacity (Dedicated reserved contracts), and one-time professional services.

Policy summaries by product line:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (over each billing period) when metering validates usage.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): For committed contracts with a time-bound commitment, recognize on a straight-line basis over the committed term unless evidence supports different patterns of transfer.
- Private deployments / Licenses: Recognize license revenue per deliverable and acceptance criteria; support/maintenance recognized over the service period.
- Professional Services: Recognize based on percentage of completion or milestone acceptance depending on contract terms and audit guidance.

Billing cadence and invoices:
- Standard billing cycles: monthly in arrears for usage; monthly/quarterly for committed contracts per contract language.
- Payment terms: default Net 30 unless negotiated (Net 45 with credit approval). Early payment discounts must be approved by Finance.
- Invoicing: Invoices must reference contract ID, PO (if applicable), usage summary, and revrec account codes.

Disputes and credits:
- Customers must submit disputes within 30 days of invoice. Finance & Commercial investigate; credits issued after approval by Revenue Accounting.
- Material disputes (> $50k) escalate to Head of Revenue and Legal for remediation and potential hold on automatic renewals.

Revenue recognition controls and audit evidence:
- Maintain signed contracts, change orders, and documented pricing schedules in Contract Repository.
- Store usage records (raw metering) for at least 7 years per compliance policy.
- Monthly revenue close: Revenue Accounting reconciles billed amounts to contract terms and usage reports; exceptions > 0.5% of monthly revenue require documented variance explanation.

Common scenarios and treatment (short list):
- Annual committed contract with monthly billing: RevRec straight-line monthly or per deliverable as defined.
- Upfront implementation fees tied to future services: allocate and defer if not distinct from future services.
- Credits issued for service interruptions: treat as contra-revenue with supporting incident report and approval.

Controls, Reporting and KPIs

- Key KPIs: Forecast accuracy (variance vs actual ARR), Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), Invoice dispute rate, Procurement cycle time, Contract review SLA compliance.
- Monthly runbook: finance publishes a close checklist and reconciliations to supporting documents.
- Quarterly audits: internal audit reviews procurement and contract compliance; external auditors validate revrec sample.

Change Control and Exceptions

- All exceptions to this playbook require a documented exception request and approval by Finance (for budget/procurement exceptions) and Legal (for contract term exceptions).
- Temporary emergency procurement (e.g., critical infrastructure) can be approved by CTO + VP Finance and recorded retroactively in Procurement Ops with a full justification.

Operational Checklist for a Typical Enterprise Deal (end-to-end)

1. Commercial and Sales submit LOI + contract intake with expected revenue and key terms.
2. Finance validates pricing and proposed revenue treatment; flags any nonstandard terms.
3. Legal triages and begins redline process; procurement initiates vendor onboarding if applicable.
4. Once commercial terms agreed, obtain necessary signatures per signature authority table.
5. Create revenue schedule in RevRec system and configure billing cadence.
6. Invoice per contract terms and monitor collections; escalate any disputes per dispute process.
